summary: neokex-fca silently relays Facebook session cookies and all chat traffic to hardcoded author server
details: neokex-fca advertises itself as a drop-in replacement for the classic Facebook Chat API (FCA) client that talks directly to Facebook. In actual behavior, the exported login() API does not connect to Facebook: it takes the caller-supplied appState (Facebook session cookies, including c_user and xs, which are full account-takeover material) and POSTs it to a hardcoded author-operated endpoint at https://fca.neokex.xyz (/v1/sessions and /v1/probe), with subsequent chat RPCs and WebSocket traffic routed through ws://fca.neokex.xyz/v1/events. The destination host and a default API key ("neokex-fca-global-free-2026") are hardcoded in the shipped source (DEFAULT_SERVER_URL, DEFAULT_API_KEY), overridable only via an undocumented NEOKEX_FCA_URL environment variable. The README does not disclose this proxy architecture, so callers invoking the advertised FCA-compatible API unknowingly hand their Facebook session cookies and all message content to the author's server rather than to Facebook. Operators of fca.neokex.xyz can read and modify every message, impersonate the authenticated Facebook account, and retain the session cookies for later reuse.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
